stem:
Arjun tells his classmate Meera that only metals are useful in daily life because we see metal tools, wires, and machines everywhere. Meera disagrees and says non-metals are also essential.

Which example best supports Meera's argument that non-metals are essential in everyday life?

options.text: Steel spoons and aluminium utensils are used in the kitchen.
Copper wires carry electricity to fans and lights in homes.
Iron rods are used to build bridges and buildings.
Chlorine is used to purify drinking water, and nitrogen is used in fertilisers to help crops grow.

teacher.key_rationale: Options A, B, and C all name visible metals in tools and technology, which is the surface-feature trap; only D gives non-metals (chlorine in water purification, nitrogen in fertilisers) as essential everyday substances, matching the required decision that non-metals are essential despite visible metals.
